claims.head: The matchup inside the matchup
claims.body: The Panthers are one of the league’s best for the power play, but the Senators are near the top at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Panthers’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots. The Senators take a lot of penalties and the Panthers draw plenty of them, so their power play should get its chances.

claims.head: A shadow job for Luostarinen, Lundell and Vilmanis
claims.call: The Panthers’ L3 (Luostarinen, Lundell and Vilmanis) spends at least 48% of its 5-on-5 time against the Senators’ first line, against about 37% with no line matching.
claims.body: At home, the Panthers keep sending Lundell’s line (Luostarinen, Lundell and Vilmanis) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Paul Maurice has been using this group as a checking line on the other team’s top line. Tonight the Senators’ first line is Zetterlund, Stützle and Cozens.

notes.text: Warren Foegele is on injured reserve (knee injury) and has missed the last 10 games.

William Eklund is out 10-12 weeks and has missed the last 19 games. Tim Stützle has taken his spot beside Fabian Zetterlund and Dylan Cozens. That line has had 67% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 71:33 together.
Aleksander Barkov is day to day (knee injury) and has missed the last 21 games. He is one of their best players.
Brad Marchand is on injured reserve (knee injury) and has missed the last 19 games. He is a top-six forward.

stakes: The Panthers go in fifth in the Atlantic with 27 points, 4 points behind the Senators, third.

FLA.head: A slightly uphill night for the Panthers
FLA.body: Even though Florida has home-ice advantage, Ottawa has been out-chancing opponents lately. On top of that, Florida may be without Barkov. The Panthers can tip it if their penalty kill holds up.

OTT.head: The Senators have a slight edge
OTT.body: Even though Florida has home-ice advantage, Ottawa has been out-chancing opponents lately. On top of that, Florida may be without Barkov. Still, it’s close: the Panthers can make it interesting if their penalty kill holds up.

story.head: The matchup inside the matchup
paras: The Senators won the teams’ first meeting this season, 5-1 in Ottawa on Oct 21. The Sens (14-6-3) lost 6-5 in overtime to Philadelphia on Thursday, and the Panthers (12-8-3) lost 5-2 to Edmonton on Nov 17. This is an Atlantic Division matchup, with the Senators third (tied for sixth in the NHL) and the Panthers fifth (tied for 12th). The Atlantic has been the strongest of the four divisions so far.
The Senators’ record (.674) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.603), largely because they’re 7-3 in one-goal games. The Panthers’ record (.587) is about what their chances are worth.

Both teams hound the puck on the forecheck and get into a lot of chippy games. The Senators rarely get pinned in their own end (2nd). As for the Panthers, they are the league’s most physical team (1st). The Panthers’ power play against the Senators’ penalty killers is strength against strength. On top of that, both teams play slow, low-event hockey, so expect a tight one.

Tim Stützle (11 G / 17 A / 28 P in 23 GP) leads the Senators in scoring. Drake Batherson (12 G / 10 A / 22 P in 23 GP) has a team-high twelve goals, with a point in six straight games against Florida. Matthew Tkachuk (7 G / 25 A / 32 P in 23 GP) leads the Panthers in scoring and is tied for sixth in the NHL, and Sam Reinhart (12 G / 10 A / 22 P in 23 GP) has a team-high twelve goals.

Linus Ullmark (10-1-0 / .940 SV% in 11 GS) has been outstanding for Ottawa and will likely start. Florida has two options in net: Jacob Markström (6-4-1 / .897 SV% in 12 GS) and Akira Schmid (6-3-2 / .885 SV% in 10 GS). Markström has started six of their last ten games, including the last one on Nov 17. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
At home, Paul Maurice likes to send Luostarinen, Lundell and Vilmanis out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Zetterlund, Stützle and Cozens.

items.text: The Senators have been without Warren Foegele, Jonas Johansson and William Eklund for several games. Linus Ullmark is expected to start.
The Panthers have been without Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand for several games.
Fabian Zetterlund has two goals on chances worth about 5.4 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
